segments.title: the self as seed basis
segments.note:
PROVISIONAL machine alignment by Codex, reconciled from two independent proposals. ltar na/According to is an HGM-attested grammatical construction, retained at phrase depth d3 for the opening standpoint; the separate ji ltar is part of the comparison completed by de bzhin du/similar, not a reason to remove the licensed standpoint phrase. rnams kyi and supplied those who/the idea of remain outside lexical spans. The first two kun gzhi rnam shes compounds select English foundation consciousness occurrences one and two; the third English repetition is explanatory and unwrapped. nyon yid owns afflicted mind, and dmigs pa owns focuses on/focus on without supplied participants. gnas owns place once; stay is its additional verbal realization.

The second self-awareness phrase can be defended whole at d3, but secure source-specific lexical units are retained: nga/me, tsam/simple, blo/awareness, lhan skyes/natural. All four have directly relevant HGM entries. The second nga selects the explicit quoted me, matching the source's quoted first person; the earlier of yourself is the English narrator's recast of that self-reference and remains unwrapped. This is a deliberate correspondence choice, not a claim that the earlier self-reference has no Tibetan contribution. snyam and the assertive 'o contribute to the thought/quotation construction but do not receive a fabricated separate atom or null. Supplied your and call framing are unwrapped. de nyid is the established pronominal compound, exactly that thing in this source, with de/that and nyid/exactly as tighter members; the HGM field is this very / just such (pronominal use), not an exact quotation of the English here.

Source sgo ba is preserved as stained, explicitly supported by HGM stain/stained. The base/seed/stain words are individually aligned; gzhir gyur pa'i, agentives and shifted our/we remain omitted where correspondence is distributed. C16 and ILL witnesses do not establish independent publication or ingestion history. No spelling correction or new erratum is proposed.
